title: Bare `except:` in predict endpoint silences all errors
description: `confidence` calculation at `ml_api_server.py:175-178` uses bare `except: pass` — this swallows any exception including `AttributeError`, `TypeError`, and `SystemExit`. Should be `except Exception:` at minimum.
recommendation: Replace bare `except:` with `except Exception as e: logger.debug(f"proba unavailable: {e}")`
acceptance_test_hint: `pylint backend/ml/ml_api_server.py` reports no bare-except violations

title: `OnlineLearner.update()` raises `NotImplementedError`
description: `online_learning.py:103` — `raise NotImplementedError` in the base `OnlineLearner.update()` method. Subclasses `IncrementalLearner` and `SGDIncrementalLearner` exist but the online learning system has no integration with the main inference path (`model_manager.py` or `ml_api_server.py`). The system is architecturally isolated.
recommendation: Wire `OnlineLearner` into `ModelManager.predict()` post-inference update cycle, or document explicitly that online learning is a non-activated feature with a roadmap item.
acceptance_test_hint: `model_manager.py` calls `online_learner.update(features, label)` after each prediction OR feature is marked `EXPERIMENTAL` in code and docs

title: Duplicate simplified pipeline is dead code
description: `simple_training_pipeline.py` (`"Phase 4 Testing"`) duplicates functionality of `training_pipeline.py` without being integrated into any production path. It provides its own `SimpleMLTrainingPipeline` class with the same `_load_config()` / `initialize()` flow. No import of this module found in any other file outside tests.
recommendation: Remove or merge into the main `training_pipeline.py` once Phase 4 testing is complete.
acceptance_test_hint: `grep -rn "simple_training_pipeline" backend/ --include="*.py"` returns only test references, and the module is deprecated in code comments

title: Feature computation iterates entities in a Python `for` loop — O(N×M)
description: `_compute_single_feature()` and all `_compute_*` built-ins iterate `entity_ids` one-by-one with Python loops rather than vectorized pandas operations. For 6,000 stocks, this creates 6,000 row-filter operations per feature per compute call.
recommendation: Refactor built-in feature computations to use grouped pandas operations: `price_data.groupby("ticker")["close"].last()` instead of per-ticker loops.
acceptance_test_hint: Feature computation for 6,000 tickers and 9 built-in features completes in <5 seconds on CPU

title: Operations guide references wrong model file path
description: Guide instructs `df -h backend/ml_models/` but model files are at `ml_models/` (project root) and the path `backend/ml_models/` does not exist. Same drift in `ML_QUICKSTART.md` which refers to `backend/ml_models/`.
recommendation: Update all documentation to use `ml_models/` (project root path) consistently.
acceptance_test_hint: `grep -rn "backend/ml_models" docs/ml/` returns no results

title: `_load_pytorch_model` is defined but never called
description: `model_manager.py:218-226` defines `_load_pytorch_model()` which calls `torch.load(path)` directly. The actual LSTM loader `_load_lstm_model()` at line 250 uses its own `torch.load()` inline. The standalone method is dead code.
recommendation: Remove `_load_pytorch_model()` or refactor LSTM loader to call it (after adding `weights_only=True`).
acceptance_test_hint: `grep -n "_load_pytorch_model" backend/ml/model_manager.py` shows only definition, no call sites

title: Rate limiting documented but not implemented
description: Document claims "1000 requests/minute per client" and "Burst: up to 50 requests in 10 seconds" with rate-limit headers. No rate limiting middleware (`slowapi`, `limits`, or custom) exists in `ml_api_server.py`.
recommendation: Either implement rate limiting (e.g., `slowapi`) or remove the rate limiting section from the docs.
acceptance_test_hint: `ml_api_server.py` imports `slowapi` and attaches limiter, OR docs section removed

title: Typo in docstring: "Makrdown"
description: Line 21: `" Make sure to append a Makrdown table..."` — typo "Makrdown". Minor but propagated to LLM system prompt, which affects model instruction quality.
recommendation: Fix to "Markdown".
acceptance_test_hint: String search confirms "Makrdown" absent.

title: `system_message` is assigned as a tuple, not a string
description: Line 24-26: `system_message = ("You are a researcher...", )` — trailing comma makes this a 1-element tuple. The prompt partial receives a tuple, not a string. LangChain will silently coerce it but the behavior is undefined and causes unexpected whitespace/formatting in the system message.
recommendation: Remove the trailing comma on line 26: `system_message = ("You are a researcher..." + " Make sure...")` → `system_message = "You are a researcher..." + " Make sure..."`.
acceptance_test_hint: `isinstance(system_message, str)` is true at runtime.

title: Filename typo: `aggresive_debator.py` (missing 'r' in aggressive)
description: File `aggresive_debator.py` should be `aggressive_debator.py`. The misspelling is also in `__init__.py:13` (`from .risk_mgmt.aggresive_debator import create_risky_debator`).
recommendation: Rename file to `aggressive_debator.py` and update import in `__init__.py`.
acceptance_test_hint: `find backend/TradingAgents -name "aggresive_debator.py"` returns no results.

title: `get_stock_stats_indicators_window` offline mode iterates day-by-day calling `get_stockstats_indicator` per day
description: Lines 526-535: for each day in `look_back_days`, a full stockstats DataFrame is re-computed (re-reading the CSV, wrapping, computing the indicator column) for a single row lookup. For 30-day windows this triggers 30 independent CSV reads and `stockstats.wrap` calls.
recommendation: Pre-compute the full indicator series once, then slice by date range.
acceptance_test_hint: Benchmark: `look_back_days=30` with mocked `pd.read_csv` shows 1 read call, not 30.

title: `get_reddit_global_news` uses a tqdm progress bar in a server-side call
description: `tqdm` writes to stderr and is appropriate for CLI; when the function is called from an API endpoint or background task, it pollutes server logs with progress bar ASCII sequences.
recommendation: Gate tqdm behind an optional `show_progress=False` parameter or remove it from the library function (the CLI wrapper can add it).
acceptance_test_hint: Server-side call with `show_progress=False` produces no stderr output.

title: `Toolkit._config` is a class-level mutable dict shared across all instances
description: `_config = DEFAULT_CONFIG.copy()` at class level means all `Toolkit` instances share state. Calling `Toolkit.update_config(...)` on one instance mutates the config seen by all other instances in the same process (e.g., in parallel or sequential backtests).
recommendation: Convert `_config` to an instance attribute in `__init__`; remove `update_config` classmethod, make it an instance method.
acceptance_test_hint: Two `Toolkit(config_a)` and `Toolkit(config_b)` instances have independent configs.

title: No tests for `FinancialSituationMemory`, `Toolkit`, or any analyst node
description: `test_trading_agents.py` covers `ConditionalLogic`, `Propagator`, `SignalProcessor`, `Reflector`, `AgentState`, `default_config`, and `dataflow/utils` — but has no tests for `FinancialSituationMemory.add_situations`, `get_memories`, any of the four analyst nodes, the researcher nodes, the trader node, or the risk debators. Memory and analyst logic are the highest-value components.
recommendation: Add mocked tests for `FinancialSituationMemory` (mock chromadb client), analyst node creation (mock LLM), and trader node.
acceptance_test_hint: `pytest backend/tests/unit/test_trading_agents.py -v` shows coverage >80% for `memory.py` and `analysts/`.

title: `_log_state` writes to relative path `eval_results/`
description: Line 225-232: `Path(f"eval_results/{self.ticker}/...")` is relative to whatever the current working directory is at invocation time. When called from inside the platform's backend service, the log files will be written to an unpredictable location.
recommendation: Use `config["results_dir"]` (already in config) as the base path: `Path(self.config["results_dir"]) / self.ticker / ...`.
acceptance_test_hint: Log files appear under `config["results_dir"]` regardless of CWD.

title: Unused imports: `time`, `json`
description: `import time` and `import json` appear at line 2 in `market_analyst.py`, `fundamentals_analyst.py`, `news_analyst.py`, `social_media_analyst.py`, `risk_manager.py`, `research_manager.py`, `bull_researcher.py`, `bear_researcher.py`, `aggresive_debator.py`, `conservative_debator.py`, `neutral_debator.py`, `trader.py` — none of these modules use `time` or `json` at all.
recommendation: Remove the unused imports; run `ruff check --select F401`.
acceptance_test_hint: `ruff check backend/TradingAgents/tradingagents/agents/` reports zero F401 violations.

title: `setup.py` lists `python_requires=">=3.10"` but platform requires Python 3.11+
description: Platform `pyproject.toml` and CI target Python 3.11. The TradingAgents package advertises 3.10+ compatibility but uses 3.10+ match-statement and TypedDict features that work fine on 3.11. The mismatch could allow a 3.10 install that fails against platform APIs.
recommendation: Set `python_requires=">=3.11"` in `setup.py` and `pyproject.toml` for consistency.
acceptance_test_hint: `pip install tradingagents` on Python 3.10 raises `VersionConflict`.

title: `YFinanceUtils` class methods are never called from within the subsystem
description: `YFinanceUtils.get_stock_info`, `get_company_info`, `get_stock_dividends`, `get_income_stmt`, `get_balance_sheet`, `get_cash_flow`, `get_analyst_recommendations` are defined but not referenced by any other file in `backend/TradingAgents/`. The active data path uses `get_YFin_data_online` / `get_YFin_data` functions in `interface.py` directly.
recommendation: Either integrate these methods into the toolkit or remove them; avoid maintaining dead surface area.
acceptance_test_hint: `grep -r "YFinanceUtils" backend/TradingAgents/tradingagents/ --include="*.py" | grep -v "yfin_utils.py"` returns no hits.

title: `get_YFin_data_online` parses `start_date`/`end_date` but discards the result
description: Lines 634-635: `datetime.strptime(start_date, "%Y-%m-%d")` and `datetime.strptime(end_date, "%Y-%m-%d")` are called purely for format validation but the return value is discarded. This is confusing — either raise a `ValueError` explicitly or remove the calls and let `yfinance` handle invalid dates.
recommendation: Remove the validation calls or store the result in a variable and use it.
acceptance_test_hint: `ruff check` no-op; code reader finds zero `_ = datetime.strptime(...)` confusion.

title: `fetch_top_from_category` raises `ValueError` if `max_limit < len(os.listdir(...))`
description: Line 68-71: a `ValueError` is raised if `max_limit` is less than the number of files in the category directory (used to calculate `limit_per_subreddit`). This condition fires when the number of subreddit data files exceeds `max_limit_per_day`, which is a plausible setup issue not a programming error. The error message `"REDDIT FETCHING ERROR: max limit is less than the number of files..."` is misleading.
recommendation: Either use `max(1, max_limit // n_files)` as a floor, or raise with a clearer message explaining that `max_limit_per_day` must be at least equal to the number of subreddit files in the category.
acceptance_test_hint: Calling `fetch_top_from_category("global_news", date, 1, ...)` with 5 subreddit files does not crash but returns at most 1 post.

title: `extract_phase()` is dead — superseded by `enhanced_extract_phase()` but never removed
description: `extract_phase()` at line 374 uses the old `self.extractor` (which itself has a bug per F-05-007) and is never called from `_run_standard_pipeline()`. `enhanced_extract_phase()` is called instead. The dead method also imports `DataValidator` as `self.legacy_validator` which is unused.
recommendation: Remove `extract_phase()`, `validate_extracted_data()` (line 402), and the `self.legacy_validator` / `self.aggregator` assignments in `__init__`.
acceptance_test_hint: `grep -n "extract_phase\ | validate_extracted_data" etl_orchestrator.py` returns zero hits after cleanup

title: Daily scanner stock list is hardcoded/test stub — returns only ~100 S&P stocks
description: `_get_all_stock_symbols()` at line 80 includes a comment "In production, this would query the database" and then does `return all_symbols[:100]` — hard limit of 100 tickers. The scanner claims to scan 6000+ stocks but actually scans at most 100.
recommendation: Implement the database query using `StockUniverseManager.get_all_active_tickers()` and remove the `[:100]` slice.
acceptance_test_hint: `scanner.scan_all_stocks()` receives len > 500 from `_get_all_stock_symbols()`

title: Documented Yahoo scraper rate (100/min, 60/min usage) contradicts code rate config
description: Doc states "Yahoo Finance Scraper: ~100/min, Our Usage: 60/min". `rate_limiting.py:52-57` configures `yahoo_scraper` at `rate=0.083` tokens/sec = 5/min with `max_per_hour=300` and `min_delay=2.0s`. Actual configured rate is 12x lower than documented.
recommendation: Update doc to match code, or update code to match intended design with explanation of the discrepancy.
acceptance_test_hint: Grep `rate_limiting.py` for `yahoo_scraper` rate value matches what DATA_COLLECTION_SOLUTION.md states

title: No tests exist for streaming layer or daily scanner
description: `find backend/tests -name "test_stream*" -o -name "test_kafka*" -o -name "test_scanner*"` returns nothing. The Kafka producer/consumer client (350 LOC), consumer loop logic, and `DailyStockScanner` (340 LOC) have zero test coverage. These components handle real-time financial data flows and scanning for 6000+ stocks.
recommendation: Add unit tests for `KafkaProducerClient.send_message()`, `KafkaConsumerClient` message handling, and `DailyStockScanner._analyze_stock()` with mocked data sources.
acceptance_test_hint: `pytest backend/tests/unit/test_streaming.py backend/tests/unit/test_scanner.py` passes

title: Two parallel extraction architectures with duplicated `ExtractionResult`, `StockData`, and source-routing logic
description: Both `unlimited_data_extractor.py` and `multi_source_extractor.py` independently implement source routing, fallback, caching integration, and result dataclasses. `etl_orchestrator.py` uses both. This creates maintenance burden and schema drift risk (already observed in F-05-005).
recommendation: Designate one extraction engine as canonical (recommend `multi_source_extractor.py` + `rate_limiting.py` as they are more structured) and deprecate/remove the unlimited extractor stack, retaining only unique capabilities (bulk CSV download, SEC scraping).
acceptance_test_hint: `grep -rn "unlimited_data_extractor\ | unlimited_extractor_with_fallbacks" backend/` returns 0 non-test hits after consolidation

title: Unused instance variables assigned in `__init__`
description: `self.legacy_validator = DataValidator()` and `self.aggregator = DataAggregator()` are assigned but never referenced outside of `__init__`. Adds startup cost and confusion about which validator is in use.
recommendation: Remove unused assignments once `extract_phase()` dead code (F-05-010) is cleaned up.
acceptance_test_hint: `grep -n "legacy_validator\ | self\.aggregator" etl_orchestrator.py` returns 0 hits

title: `processing_task` asyncio task created but never awaited or cancelled
description: `asyncio.create_task(self.distributed_processor.start_processing())` stores result in `processing_task` but the variable is never awaited, and not cancelled in the except block. If the function returns normally, the background task may continue running.
recommendation: `await processing_task` after `stop_processing()`, or cancel it in finally block: `processing_task.cancel(); await asyncio.gather(processing_task, return_exceptions=True)`.
acceptance_test_hint: `asyncio.all_tasks()` returns empty set after `_run_distributed_pipeline` completes

title: ETL_ACTIVATION_SUCCESS.md declares "production ready" as of 2025-08-19 — fully stale
description: Entire document asserts operational readiness and successful import. As of 2026-04-27, ETL package import fails with `ModuleNotFoundError: No module named 'selenium'`. Document should be marked deprecated or replaced with current state.
recommendation: Supersede document with post-fix validation report after F-05-001 is resolved.
acceptance_test_hint: N/A — doc update

title: SQLAlchemy `QueuePool` of 10 connections created per `DataLoader` instance
description: `ETLOrchestrator` instantiates `DataLoader()` at construction. If multiple orchestrators or tasks run concurrently, each creates its own pool of 10. A singleton or dependency-injected engine would prevent connection overuse.
recommendation: Promote engine to module-level singleton or accept it as a constructor parameter.
acceptance_test_hint: `DataLoader._create_engine` is called exactly once per process lifetime in integration test

title: Hardcoded user-agent rotation list is stale (Chrome 91/92, Firefox 89, Safari 14.1 from 2021)
description: `_get_random_user_agent()` at line 37 returns one of 5 user-agent strings, all from 2021. Modern anti-bot systems flag outdated user-agents.
recommendation: Source from a maintained user-agent library (`fake-useragent` or `ua-generator`) or update the list periodically via config.
acceptance_test_hint: Manual check: scrapers do not receive HTTP 403 from Yahoo Finance endpoints in staging

title: `ensure_pool_exists()` runs at DAG parse time, not task time
description: `ensure_pool_exists()` is called at module level (line 1572), meaning it executes on every DAG parse cycle (typically every 30 seconds). This opens a database session repeatedly, adding unnecessary load to the metadata DB and potentially causing parse slowdowns.
recommendation: Move pool creation to a dedicated setup task or, preferably, provision the pool via infrastructure-as-code (e.g., Airflow CLI in a Kubernetes init container or Terraform).
acceptance_test_hint: Removing the top-level call and instead calling it inside a `@dag` factory or init task results in no pool creation calls during DAG file parsing.

title: `OrchestratorConfig.__dict__` not JSON-serializable for XCom
description: `context['task_instance'].xcom_push(key='orchestrator_config', value=config.__dict__)` at line 162 pushes a dict containing `retraining_triggers` — a list of `RetrainingTrigger` dataclass instances. Dataclasses are not JSON-serializable by default; on Airflow XCom backends that require JSON (e.g., custom XCom backends, Airflow 2.7+ with `enable_xcom_pickling=False`), this will raise `TypeError`. The value is never pulled back by any downstream task (unused XCom).
recommendation: Either delete the push (it is unused) or serialize properly with `dataclasses.asdict(config)`.
acceptance_test_hint: `grep -n "xcom_pull.*orchestrator_config" data_pipelines/airflow/dags/ml_training_pipeline_dag.py` returns no hits after removal; no `TypeError` in task logs.

title: `data_count >= 20` threshold is inconsistent with declared `MIN_DATA_POINTS = 26`
description: `calculate_indicators_parallel` (line 666) and `calculate_indicators_batch` (line 1356) filter with `data_count >= 20`. The `TechnicalIndicatorsCalculator` class (utils) declares `MIN_DATA_POINTS = 26` with the comment "Needed for EMA-26". Using 20 means EMA-26 calculations for stocks with 20-25 data points will produce inaccurate values (they are calculated over a shorter window than 26 periods).
recommendation: Change `AND data_count >= 20` in both CTE WHERE clauses to `AND data_count >= 26` (matching the documented minimum), or update `MIN_DATA_POINTS` comment if 20 is intentional.
acceptance_test_hint: All three locations where the threshold appears read `>= 26`; unit test asserts EMA-26 values are `NULL` for stocks with fewer than 26 data points.

title: `BashOperator` and `ExternalTaskSensor` imported but never used
description: Both `BashOperator` (line 25) and `ExternalTaskSensor` (line 26) are imported but appear nowhere in task definitions or function bodies — confirmed by `grep` returning only the import lines. In addition to the dead import issue, their 1.x import paths will raise `ImportError` on Airflow 2.x before being used.
recommendation: Remove both unused import lines entirely.
acceptance_test_hint: `grep -n "BashOperator\ | ExternalTaskSensor" data_pipelines/airflow/dags/ml_training_pipeline_dag.py` returns no hits.

title: EMA approximation using SMA is documented as "EMA" but produces SMA values
description: The SQL CTE `rsi_calc` in both `calculate_indicators_parallel` and `calculate_indicators_batch` computes `ema_12` and `ema_26` using simple `AVG()` window functions (SMA), not exponential weighting. Comments in `technical_indicators_calculator.py` (line 244) acknowledge this as "EMA approximation", but the column names `ema_12`/`ema_26` stored in `technical_indicators` imply true EMA to consumers (e.g., the recommendation scoring in `score_stock`). A true recursive EMA SQL implementation is already provided in `EMA_RECURSIVE_SQL` in the utils file but is unused.
recommendation: At minimum add a column comment in the `technical_indicators` table DDL noting values are SMA approximations. Consider adopting the recursive CTE (`EMA_RECURSIVE_SQL`) already authored in `technical_indicators_calculator.py:585-626`.
acceptance_test_hint: Documentation or table comment reflects approximation nature; or `EMA_RECURSIVE_SQL` is integrated.

title: `asyncio.new_event_loop` / `set_event_loop` is an anti-pattern in Python 3.10+
description: `run_etl_pipeline` and `run_incremental_update` use `asyncio.new_event_loop()` + `asyncio.set_event_loop(loop)` then `loop.run_until_complete(...)`. On Python 3.10+ the preferred idiom is `asyncio.run(coro)`, which handles loop creation and cleanup correctly, avoids event loop leaks if an exception occurs before `loop.close()`, and does not pollute the thread's event loop slot.
recommendation: Replace `loop = asyncio.new_event_loop(); asyncio.set_event_loop(loop); try: result = loop.run_until_complete(...); finally: loop.close()` with `result = asyncio.run(...)`.
acceptance_test_hint: `grep -n "new_event_loop\ | set_event_loop" data_pipelines/airflow/dags/enhanced_stock_pipeline.py` returns no hits.

title: `RecommendationEngine` and `OptimizedRecommendationEngine` duplicate the daily pipeline
description: Both classes implement `generate_daily_recommendations` with similar logic but different batching strategies. `RecommendationEngine` has no caching, `OptimizedRecommendationEngine` has full BoundedDict caching. When the optimized engine is broken (F-09-002), callers fall through to the original which has no memory bounds on large universes.
recommendation: Make `RecommendationEngine` the thin interface and delegate implementation to the optimized engine (or vice versa via strategy pattern).
acceptance_test_hint: Single code path for daily recommendation generation

title: `get_top_sectors` hardcodes `"Technology"` for all tickers
description: All recommendations are tagged as Technology sector regardless of actual sector data. The `StockRecommendation` dataclass has no `sector` field. The report summary will always show only one sector.
recommendation: Either add `sector: Optional[str] = None` to `StockRecommendation` and populate it from market scanner data, or remove `top_sectors` from the report until sector data is available.
acceptance_test_hint: `get_top_sectors` returns varied sector values for a mixed-sector list

title: `generate_report` with `format='pdf'` and `format='excel'` are stubs returning `None`
description: Both `format='pdf'` and `format='excel'` branches contain `pass` and return `None`. API callers that request these formats receive a `None` response with no error.
recommendation: Implement PDF/Excel generation or raise `NotImplementedError("PDF/Excel format not yet supported")` to prevent silent failures.
acceptance_test_hint: `generate_report(recs, format='pdf')` raises `NotImplementedError`

title: ADF test statistic approximation is incorrect for cointegration residuals
description: The custom ADF implementation computes `rho * sqrt(n)` from Pearson correlation, which is not the ADF tau statistic. The correct ADF tau is `beta / se(beta)` from the OLS regression of `delta_spread ~ spread_lag`. Critical values for cointegration residuals also differ from standard ADF tables. This produces unreliable cointegration decisions.
recommendation: Replace with `statsmodels.tsa.stattools.adfuller(spread, regression='nc')` for correct ADF statistics and p-values.
acceptance_test_hint: `test_cointegration` p-value matches `adfuller` output for the same residual series

title: O(n²) SMA calculation in `_analyze_market_structure`
description: SMA20, SMA50, and SMA200 are computed via list comprehensions using `np.mean(close[max(0,i-k):i+1])` for every `i` in the array — O(n) per point, O(n²) total. For 500-stock batch analysis this is a bottleneck.
recommendation: Replace with `pd.Series(close).rolling(k).mean().values` (O(n) via cumsum).
acceptance_test_hint: `_analyze_market_structure` runtime on 500-row array < 10ms

title: `_calculate_obv` and `_calculate_ad_line` use Python loops over numpy arrays
description: Both functions iterate element-by-element in pure Python, bypassing numpy vectorisation. For a stock with 500 data points each call is ~50x slower than a vectorised equivalent.
recommendation: Replace loops with `np.where` / `np.cumsum` patterns. For OBV: `obv_changes = np.where(close[1:]>close[:-1], volume[1:], np.where(close[1:]<close[:-1], -volume[1:], 0)); obv = np.cumsum(obv_changes)[-1]`.
acceptance_test_hint: Unit test runtime for `_calculate_volume_indicators` on 500-row data < 5ms

title: `VaRCalculator` has no unit tests in scope
description: No test file specifically covers `VaRCalculator` — `test_risk_manager.py` covers `backend/utils/risk_manager.py`, not this calculator. The Kupiec backtest, Monte Carlo, and CVaR paths are untested.
recommendation: Add `backend/tests/unit/test_var_calculator.py` with parametrised tests for historical, parametric, and Monte Carlo methods including the `backtest_var` Kupiec test.
acceptance_test_hint: `pytest backend/tests/unit/test_var_calculator.py` passes with ≥80% branch coverage

title: `BlackLittermanOptimizer` has no unit tests
description: No test file covers the Black-Litterman model. The posterior weight normalisation (`posterior_weights / np.sum(np.abs(posterior_weights))` at line 117) can produce negative weights when posterior returns are mixed-sign, but this is never validated.
recommendation: Add tests for zero-view case, single-view case, and verify weight normalisation produces positive-sum results.
acceptance_test_hint: `pytest backend/tests/unit/test_black_litterman.py` passes

title: `SentimentAnalysisEngine.analyze_sentiment` docstring/API contract mismatch
description: The class docstring says "Uses FinBERT (ProsusAI/finbert) as primary analyzer", but the public `analyze_sentiment` method accepts a single `text: str`. The higher-level `_run_sentiment_analysis` in `recommendation_engine.py` passes `(ticker, list_of_dicts)` — indicating caller-side confusion about the contract.
recommendation: Document the intended call sites clearly. Add `analyze_stock_sentiment(ticker, texts)` to the public interface in the class docstring and mark `analyze_sentiment(text)` as the low-level single-text API.
acceptance_test_hint: Module docstring accurately describes both public methods

title: Private shim methods inflate class by ~50 lines
description: `RecommendationEngine` defines 15+ thin `_method` shims that simply delegate to imported module-level functions (e.g. `def _normalize_score(self, ...): return normalize_score(...)`). These exist "for unit tests patching internals" but make the class larger and harder to navigate.
recommendation: Remove shims and update any test that patches them to patch at the module level.
acceptance_test_hint: `RecommendationEngine` class body < 300 lines

title: Duplicate `_calculate_max_drawdown` exists here and in multiple other files
description: `PortfolioOptimizer._calculate_max_drawdown` is essentially the same logic as `RecommendationEngine._calculate_risk_metrics` drawdown computation and the version in `recommendation_scoring.py`.
recommendation: Extract to `backend/analytics/risk/calculators/drawdown.py` and import uniformly.
acceptance_test_hint: Single implementation referenced by all three callers
